episodes.content: I want to put $200K into the SpaceX IPO. I have about 6 days to decide. What would that do to my taxes and my income plan? Explain it like I'm not a finance person, please. I know we've been spending more the last few months, and the lake house is still the big one for us — I'd still want to keep the grandkids' 529s on track. Most of what I could sell quickly is between my old 401k and the Robinhood account.

We walked through where $200K could come from — cash and money market (~$206K available, essentially no tax), selling the Apple position in your trust (~$170K, with an estimated $18,500 in capital-gains tax but it would also reduce your single-stock concentration), or selling Robinhood holdings (~$96K, an estimated $14,500 tax on very low-basis tech shares). We also looked at what a $200K illiquid position means for your $9,000/mo income plan while spending is running ~18% above plan. You said you hate the idea of paying tax on the Apple you bought back in 2015. We ended with a list of questions to bring to Dana before the June 15 deadline.
